messages:
Anita: Quick sync — we need a concrete plan for capacity-driven variant fallback. Primary goal: keep gold/paid latency SLOs, avoid cross-region hops unless unavoidable. Thoughts on policy shape?
Mike: +1. My instinct: prefer same-region compatible variants first (quantized, lower seq length), then regional warm-pool, finally remote fallback. For free tier, prefer local smaller model or 429.
Carolina: Agreed. Also we should consider per-tenant budgets so we don't erode reserved capacity for dedicated customers. If tenant has dedicated slots, fallback should respect that.
Josh: Question — how do we detect "saturated"? Instant queue length? p95 queueing? token throughput drop? Need a single canonical signal for the router.
Lee: Propose a composite "capacity_pressure_score" = weighted(queue_len, cpu_util, pending_requests_rate, kv-cache-miss-rate). Thresholds: 0.7 for probe, 0.9 for immediate diversion.
Anita: Love the score approach. When score >= 0.7, router should start lightweight sampling to compatible variants with a handshake probe (single-request probe) rather than full divert. If probes succeed we gradually increase diversion pct.
Mike: Implementation note: probes must carry a header so we can measure accuracy and user-visible latency deltas: `X-Fallback-Probe: true` and `X-Fallback-Orig-Model: rtx-4k`. We log both responses.
Carolina: Console UX — ops teams want an explicit toggle per-tenant: fallback_policy = { mode: "auto_probe", max_remote_pct: 10, prefer_same_region: true }. Also surface realtime "fallback_rate" and "avg_delta_ms" on tenant dashboard.
Josh: Telemetry list: fallback_attempts, fallback_success_rate, fallback_latency_delta_p50/p95, fallback_error_rate_by_variant, probe_success_rate. Add learnable alerts: alert if fallback success_rate < 50% for 15m.
Lee: Backoff algorithm: exponential backoff with jitter per-tenant per-variant, 3 successful probes to promote, 5 failures to demote. Sticky routing for session TTL=30s to avoid flapping.
Anita: Policy API design suggestion: POST /routing/policies { "tenant": "t-123", "policy": "capacity_based", "params": { "probe_threshold": 0.7, "divert_threshold": 0.9, "max_divert_pct": 20 }}
Mike: Can we use a preference header instead of changing API shape? `X-Model-Preference: prefer=compatible;fallback=allowed;max_remote=5` This keeps per-request overrides for SDKs.
Carolina: Both. API policy for defaults + request header for overrides (with tenant-level guardrails). Console exposes the default and logs when request-level overrides used.
Josh: Ops playbook: on high fallback_rate, run quick checks — 1) variant health, 2) regional capacity, 3) unexpected request pattern. Add runbook link in alert.
Lee: Dev detail — router should maintain a tiny probe cache to avoid over-probing. If variant recently probed within 10s, reuse result. Also, prefer quantized variants that preserve logits mapping to reduce quality regressions.
Anita: Risk: silent quality regressions for users. Mitigation: route small percent of live traffic (canaries) through fallback and run automated prompt-level evals; integrate with Redwood Optimize to flag regressions.
Mike: Rollout plan: 1) feature-flagged impl only for internal tenants, 2) enable for small group of customers with console opt-in, 3) wide rollout with per-tenant opt-out.
Carolina: Dashboard widgets: 1) fallback funnel (probe -> diverted -> success), 2) latency delta histogram, 3) capacity_pressure heatmap by region & tier.
Anita: Ops-bot, can you add a quick check that posts `capacity_pressure_score` per-region every 5m into ops channel?
ops-bot: scheduled: posting `capacity_pressure_score` for regions: us-west=0.42, eu-central=0.76 (probe), ap-south=0.21.
Mike: Small API nuance — we should tag diverted requests with a deterministic reason code: `divert:pressure_region`, `divert:quota_exceeded`, `divert:tenant_override`. That makes telemetry queries simpler.
Josh: One last on SLA: for enterprise (reserved) tenants we should never divert off their dedicated pool unless explicit admin policy. Add a hard-exclusion flag.
Carolina: Agree. We'll add `hard_exclusion=true` to tenant config. Console will show a lock icon for protected tenants.
Lee: I'll prototype router changes and a probe harness this week. Will push a design PR with config schema and sample metrics.
Anita: Perfect. Next steps: Lee opens design PR, Mike drafts API header spec, Carolina drafts console widgets + alert definitions, Josh writes runbook. We'll reconvene Friday to validate metrics and mock dashboard. :thumbsup:
